summary: Large and small language models have been widely used for robotic task planning. At the same time, vision-language models (VLMs) have successfully tackled problems such as image captioning, scene understanding, and visual question answering. In this work, we combine these two approaches by deploying a compact, open-source multimodal model to generate behavior trees for robotic task planning. The main obstacle to achieving this goal is the lack of an existing dataset that links visual observations and instructions to executable behavior trees. We propose a method to construct such a dataset starting from existing robotic episodes (i.e., Open X-Embodiment), in which a large model serves as a teacher in a multi-stage generation pipeline. We use this dataset to fine-tune VLMs ranging from 500M to 4B parameters via parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). The generated behavior trees, compatible with the BehaviorTree.CPP library, are evaluated both offline, using structural and lexical metrics, and online through the execution of household tasks in a state-of-the-art embodied simulator. Our results demonstrate that our fine-tuned 4B-parameter VLM approaches the performance of state-of-the-art closed-source models, achieving an 87\% success rate while requiring only a fraction of the computational resources.

AI.tldr: A compact open-source multimodal model is fine-tuned to generate executable behavior trees for robotic task planning from visual observations and instructions, achieving 87% success rate with minimal computational resources.
AI.motivation: To combine the strengths of language models for robotic task planning and vision-language models for scene understanding by creating a system that can generate executable behavior trees from visual observations and instructions, addressing the lack of existing datasets linking these elements.
AI.method: Construct a dataset from existing robotic episodes (Open X-Embodiment) using a large model as teacher in a multi-stage generation pipeline. Fine-tune VLMs (500M to 4B parameters) via parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) to generate BehaviorTree.CPP-compatible behavior trees.
AI.result: The fine-tuned 4B-parameter VLM approaches state-of-the-art closed-source model performance with 87% success rate on household tasks in an embodied simulator, while requiring only a fraction of computational resources. Offline evaluation shows strong structural and lexical metrics.
AI.conclusion: Compact open-source multimodal models can effectively generate executable behavior trees for robotic task planning, achieving competitive performance with minimal computational requirements, enabling more accessible and efficient robotic planning systems.

title: Sticky-Glance: Robust Intent Recognition for Human Robot Collaboration via Single-Glance
summary: Gaze is a valuable means of communication for impaired people with extremely limited motor capabilities. However, robust gaze-based intent recognition in multi-object environments is challenging due to gaze noise, micro-saccades, viewpoint changes, and dynamic objects. To address this, we propose an object-centric gaze grounding framework that stabilizes intent through a sticky-glance algorithm, jointly modeling geometric distance and direction trends. The inferred intent remains anchored to the object even under short glances with minimal 3 gaze samples, achieving a tracking rate of 0.94 for dynamic targets and selection accuracy of 0.98 for static targets. We further introduce a continuous shared control and multi-modal interaction paradigm, enabling high-readiness control and human-in-loop feedback, thereby reducing task duration for nearly 10 \%. Experiments across dynamic tracking, multi-perspective alignment, a baseline comparison, user studies, and ablation studies demonstrate improved robustness, efficiency, and reduced workload compared to representative baselines.

AI.tldr: Object-centric gaze grounding framework with sticky-glance algorithm for robust intent recognition in multi-object environments, achieving high tracking/selection accuracy and reducing task duration.
AI.motivation: Gaze is valuable for impaired people with limited motor capabilities, but robust gaze-based intent recognition is challenging due to gaze noise, micro-saccades, viewpoint changes, and dynamic objects.
AI.method: Propose object-centric gaze grounding framework with sticky-glance algorithm that jointly models geometric distance and direction trends to stabilize intent; introduce continuous shared control and multi-modal interaction paradigm.
AI.result: Achieves tracking rate of 0.94 for dynamic targets and selection accuracy of 0.98 for static targets with minimal 3 gaze samples; reduces task duration by nearly 10%; demonstrates improved robustness, efficiency, and reduced workload.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables high-readiness control and human-in-loop feedback, providing robust gaze-based intent recognition for impaired users in complex multi-object environments.

title: Dual-Agent Multiple-Model Reinforcement Learning for Event-Triggered Human-Robot Co-Adaptation in Decoupled Task Spaces
summary: This paper presents a shared-control rehabilitation policy for a custom 6-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) upper-limb robot that decomposes complex reaching tasks into decoupled spatial axes. The patient governs the primary reaching direction using binary commands, while the robot autonomously manages orthogonal corrective motions. Because traditional fixed-frequency control often induces trajectory oscillations due to variable inverse-kinematics execution times, an event-driven progression strategy is proposed. This architecture triggers subsequent control actions only when the end-effector enters an admission sphere centred on the immediate target waypoint, and was validated in a semi-virtual setup linking a physical pressure sensor to a MuJoCo simulation. To optimise human--robot co-adaptation safely and efficiently, this study introduces Dual Agent Multiple Model Reinforcement Learning (DAMMRL). This framework discretises decision characteristics: the human agent selects the admission sphere radius to reflect their inherent speed--accuracy trade-off, while the robot agent dynamically adjusts its 3D Cartesian step magnitudes to complement the user's cognitive state. Trained in simulation and deployed across mixed environments, this event-triggered DAMMRL approach effectively suppresses waypoint chatter, balances spatial precision with temporal efficiency, and significantly improves success rates in object acquisition tasks.

AI.tldr: Event-driven shared-control rehabilitation policy using DAMMRL for 6-DoF upper-limb robots that decomposes reaching tasks, suppresses trajectory oscillations, and optimizes human-robot co-adaptation.
AI.motivation: Traditional fixed-frequency control in upper-limb rehabilitation robots causes trajectory oscillations due to variable inverse-kinematics execution times, requiring a more adaptive approach to improve human-robot interaction and task success.
AI.method: Proposes event-driven progression with admission spheres and Dual Agent Multiple Model Reinforcement Learning (DAMMRL) where human selects sphere radius (speed-accuracy trade-off) and robot adjusts 3D Cartesian step magnitudes, validated in semi-virtual MuJoCo simulation.
AI.result: Effectively suppresses waypoint chatter, balances spatial precision with temporal efficiency, and significantly improves success rates in object acquisition tasks across mixed environments.
AI.conclusion: The event-triggered DAMMRL approach provides an effective framework for shared-control rehabilitation that optimizes human-robot co-adaptation while maintaining safety and efficiency in complex reaching tasks.

title: DreamToNav: Generalizable Navigation for Robots via Generative Video Planning
summary: We present DreamToNav, a novel autonomous robot framework that uses generative video models to enable intuitive, human-in-the-loop control. Instead of relying on rigid waypoint navigation, users provide natural language prompts (e.g. ``Follow the person carefully''), which the system translates into executable motion. Our pipeline first employs Qwen 2.5-VL-7B-Instruct to refine vague user instructions into precise visual descriptions. These descriptions condition NVIDIA Cosmos 2.5, a state-of-the-art video foundation model, to synthesize a physically consistent video sequence of the robot performing the task. From this synthetic video, we extract a valid kinematic path using visual pose estimation, robot detection and trajectory recovery. By treating video generation as a planning engine, DreamToNav allows robots to visually "dream" complex behaviors before executing them, providing a unified framework for obstacle avoidance and goal-directed navigation without task-specific engineering. We evaluate the approach on both a wheeled mobile robot and a quadruped robot in indoor navigation tasks. DreamToNav achieves a success rate of 76.7%, with final goal errors typically within 0.05-0.10 m and trajectory tracking errors below 0.15 m. These results demonstrate that trajectories extracted from generative video predictions can be reliably executed on physical robots across different locomotion platforms.

AI.tldr: DreamToNav is an autonomous robot framework that uses generative video models to translate natural language prompts into executable robot motion, allowing robots to "dream" behaviors before execution.
AI.motivation: To enable intuitive, human-in-the-loop control of robots without relying on rigid waypoint navigation, allowing users to provide natural language instructions instead of technical specifications.
AI.method: Pipeline uses Qwen 2.5-VL-7B-Instruct to refine vague instructions into precise visual descriptions, then conditions NVIDIA Cosmos 2.5 video foundation model to synthesize physically consistent videos of robot performing tasks. From synthetic videos, extracts kinematic paths using visual pose estimation, robot detection, and trajectory recovery.
AI.result: Achieves 76.7% success rate on indoor navigation tasks with wheeled mobile robot and quadruped robot. Final goal errors typically within 0.05-0.10 m and trajectory tracking errors below 0.15 m.
AI.conclusion: Trajectories extracted from generative video predictions can be reliably executed on physical robots across different locomotion platforms, providing a unified framework for obstacle avoidance and goal-directed navigation without task-specific engineering.

title: KISS-IMU: Self-supervised Inertial Odometry with Motion-balanced Learning and Uncertainty-aware Inference
summary: Inertial measurement units (IMUs), which provide high-frequency linear acceleration and angular velocity measurements, serve as fundamental sensing modalities in robotic systems. Recent advances in deep neural networks have led to remarkable progress in inertial odometry. However, the heavy reliance on ground truth data during training fundamentally limits scalability and generalization to unseen and diverse environments. We propose KISS-IMU, a novel self-supervised inertial odometry framework that eliminates ground truth dependency by leveraging simple LiDAR-based ICP registration and pose graph optimization as a supervisory signal. Our approach embodies two key principles: keeping the IMU stable through motion-aware balanced training and keeping the IMU strong through uncertainty-driven adaptive weighting during inference. To evaluate performance across diverse motion patterns and scenarios, we conducted comprehensive experiments on various real-world platforms, including quadruped robots. Importantly, we train only the IMU network in a self-supervised manner, with LiDAR serving solely as a lightweight supervisory signal rather than requiring additional learnable processes. This design enables the framework to ensure robustness without relying on joint multi-modal learning or ground truth supervision. The supplementary materials are available at https://sparolab.github.io/research/kiss_imu.

AI.tldr: KISS-IMU is a self-supervised inertial odometry framework that eliminates ground truth dependency by using LiDAR-based ICP registration and pose graph optimization as supervisory signals, with motion-aware balanced training and uncertainty-driven adaptive weighting.
AI.motivation: Current deep learning approaches for inertial odometry heavily rely on ground truth data during training, which fundamentally limits scalability and generalization to unseen and diverse environments. There's a need for methods that can learn from unlabeled data while maintaining robustness across various motion patterns and scenarios.
AI.method: The framework uses LiDAR-based ICP registration and pose graph optimization as a supervisory signal for self-supervised training of the IMU network. It employs two key principles: 1) keeping the IMU stable through motion-aware balanced training, and 2) keeping the IMU strong through uncertainty-driven adaptive weighting during inference. The LiDAR serves only as a lightweight supervisory signal without requiring additional learnable processes.
AI.result: Comprehensive experiments were conducted on various real-world platforms including quadruped robots, demonstrating performance across diverse motion patterns and scenarios. The framework shows robustness without relying on joint multi-modal learning or ground truth supervision.
AI.conclusion: KISS-IMU successfully eliminates ground truth dependency in inertial odometry training while maintaining robustness across diverse environments. The self-supervised approach using LiDAR as a lightweight supervisory signal enables scalable learning without the limitations of ground truth data collection.

title: Few-Shot Neural Differentiable Simulator: Real-to-Sim Rigid-Contact Modeling
summary: Accurate physics simulation is essential for robotic learning and control, yet analytical simulators often fail to capture complex contact dynamics, while learning-based simulators typically require large amounts of costly real-world data. To bridge this gap, we propose a few-shot real-to-sim approach that combines the physical consistency of analytical formulations with the representational capacity of graph neural network (GNN)-based models. Using only a small amount of real-world data, our method calibrates analytical simulators to generate large-scale synthetic datasets that capture diverse contact interactions. On this foundation, we introduce a mesh-based GNN that implicitly models rigid-body forward dynamics and derive surrogate gradients for collision detection, achieving full differentiability. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach enables learning-based simulators to outperform differentiable baselines in replicating real-world trajectories. In addition, the differentiable design supports gradient-based optimization, which we validate through simulation-based policy learning in multi-object interaction scenarios. Extensive experiments show that our framework not only improves simulation fidelity with minimal supervision but also increases the efficiency of policy learning. Taken together, these findings suggest that differentiable simulation with few-shot real-world grounding provides a powerful direction for advancing future robotic manipulation and control.

AI.tldr: A few-shot real-to-sim approach combines analytical physics with GNNs to create differentiable simulators using minimal real data, improving simulation fidelity and policy learning efficiency.
AI.motivation: Analytical simulators fail to capture complex contact dynamics, while learning-based simulators require large amounts of costly real-world data. There's a need to bridge this gap with physically consistent yet data-efficient simulation methods.
AI.method: Proposes a few-shot real-to-sim approach that: 1) calibrates analytical simulators with small real-world data to generate large-scale synthetic datasets, 2) introduces a mesh-based GNN that implicitly models rigid-body forward dynamics, and 3) derives surrogate gradients for collision detection to achieve full differentiability.
AI.result: The approach enables learning-based simulators to outperform differentiable baselines in replicating real-world trajectories. The differentiable design supports gradient-based optimization, validated through simulation-based policy learning in multi-object interaction scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Differentiable simulation with few-shot real-world grounding provides a powerful direction for advancing robotic manipulation and control, improving simulation fidelity with minimal supervision and increasing policy learning efficiency.

title: Towards Robotic Lake Maintenance: Integrating SONAR and Satellite Data to Assist Human Operators
comment: Accepted to and presented at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Robotics Engineering (ICMRE)
summary: Artificial Water Bodies (AWBs) are human-made systems that require continuous monitoring due to their artificial biological processes. These systems demand regular maintenance to manage their ecosystems effectively. As a result of these artificial conditions, underwater vegetation can grow rapidly and must be harvested to preserve the ecological balance. This paper proposes a two-step approach to support targeted weed harvesting for the maintenance of artificial lakes. The first step is the initial detection of Submerged Aquatic Vegetation (SAV), also referred to in this paper as areas of interest, is performed using satellite-derived indices, specifically the Aquatic Plants and Algae (APA) index, which highlights submerged vegetation in water bodies. Subsequently, an Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) equipped with multibeam SOund NAvigation and Ranging (SONAR) performs high-resolution bathymetric mapping to locate and quantify aquatic vegetation precisely. This two-stage approach offers an effective human-robot collaboration, where satellite data guides the USV missions and boat skippers leverage detailed SONAR maps for targeted harvesting. This setup narrows the search space and reduces manual workload from human operators, making the harvesting process less labour-intensive for operators. Preliminary results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating satellite imagery and underwater acoustic sensing to improve vegetation management in artificial lakes.

AI.tldr: Two-stage approach combining satellite-derived APA index for initial SAV detection with USV-mounted multibeam SONAR for precise mapping, enabling targeted weed harvesting in artificial lakes through human-robot collaboration.
AI.motivation: Artificial Water Bodies (AWBs) require continuous monitoring and maintenance due to rapid underwater vegetation growth that must be harvested to preserve ecological balance, necessitating more efficient methods than manual approaches.
AI.method: Two-step approach: 1) Initial detection of Submerged Aquatic Vegetation (SAV) using satellite-derived Aquatic Plants and Algae (APA) index to identify areas of interest; 2) High-resolution bathymetric mapping using Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) equipped with multibeam SONAR for precise vegetation location and quantification.
AI.result: Preliminary results demonstrate feasibility of integrating satellite imagery and underwater acoustic sensing for vegetation management, enabling targeted harvesting that narrows search space and reduces manual workload for operators.
AI.conclusion: The proposed human-robot collaboration system effectively supports targeted weed harvesting in artificial lakes by combining satellite guidance with detailed SONAR mapping, making vegetation management less labor-intensive while maintaining ecological balance.

title: SuperSuit: An Isomorphic Bimodal Interface for Scalable Mobile Manipulation
summary: High-quality, long-horizon demonstrations are essential for embodied AI, yet acquiring such data for tightly coupled wheeled mobile manipulators remains a fundamental bottleneck. Unlike fixed-base systems, mobile manipulators require continuous coordination between $SE(2)$ locomotion and precise manipulation, exposing limitations in existing teleoperation and wearable interfaces. We present \textbf{SuperSuit}, a bimodal data acquisition framework that supports both robot-in-the-loop teleoperation and active demonstration under a shared kinematic interface. Both modalities produce structurally identical joint-space trajectories, enabling direct data mixing without modifying downstream policies. For locomotion, SuperSuit maps natural human stepping to continuous planar base velocities, eliminating discrete command switches. For manipulation, it employs a strictly isomorphic wearable arm in both modes, while policy training is formulated in a shift-invariant delta-joint representation to mitigate calibration offsets and structural compliance without inverse kinematics. Real-world experiments on long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks show 2.6$\times$ higher demonstration throughput in active mode compared to a teleoperation baseline, comparable policy performance when substituting teleoperation data with active demonstrations at fixed dataset size, and monotonic performance improvement as active data volume increases. These results indicate that consistent kinematic representations across collection modalities enable scalable data acquisition for long-horizon mobile manipulation.

AI.tldr: SuperSuit is a bimodal data acquisition framework for mobile manipulators that supports both teleoperation and active demonstration using consistent kinematic representations, enabling scalable collection of long-horizon demonstrations.
AI.motivation: Acquiring high-quality, long-horizon demonstrations for wheeled mobile manipulators is challenging due to the need for continuous coordination between SE(2) locomotion and precise manipulation. Existing teleoperation and wearable interfaces have limitations for these tightly coupled systems.
AI.method: SuperSuit uses a bimodal framework with shared kinematic interface for both robot-in-the-loop teleoperation and active demonstration. It maps human stepping to continuous planar base velocities for locomotion, employs isomorphic wearable arm for manipulation, and uses shift-invariant delta-joint representation for policy training to handle calibration offsets and structural compliance.
AI.result: Active mode achieves 2.6× higher demonstration throughput than teleoperation baseline. Policies trained with active demonstrations perform comparably to those trained with teleoperation data at fixed dataset size, with monotonic performance improvement as active data volume increases.
AI.conclusion: Consistent kinematic representations across collection modalities enable scalable data acquisition for long-horizon mobile manipulation, with active demonstrations providing higher throughput while maintaining policy performance.

title: Open-Source Based and ETSI Compliant Cooperative, Connected, and Automated Mini-Cars
summary: The automotive sector is following a revolutionary path from vehicles controlled by humans to vehicles that will be fully automated, fully connected, and ultimately fully cooperative. Along this road, new cooperative algorithms and protocols will be designed and field tested, which represents a great challenge in terms of costs. In this context, in particular, moving from simulations to practical experiments requires huge investments that are not always affordable and may become a barrier in some cases. To solve this issue and provide the community with an intermediate step, we here propose the use of 1:10 scaled cooperative, autonomous, and connected mini-cars. The mini-car is equipped with a Jetson Orin board running the open Robot Operating System 2 (ROS2), sensors for autonomous operations, and a Raspberry Pi board for connectivity mounting the open source Open Stack for Car (OScar). A key aspect of the proposal is the use of OScar, which implements a full ETSI cooperative-intelligent transport systems (C-ITS) compliant stack. The feasibility and potential of the proposed platform is here demonstrated through the implementation of a case study where the Day-1 intersection collision warning (ICW) application is implemented and validated.

AI.tldr: Proposes using 1:10 scaled autonomous mini-cars with ROS2 and OScar (ETSI C-ITS compliant stack) as an affordable intermediate step between simulation and full-scale testing for cooperative vehicle algorithms.
AI.motivation: The transition from simulation to practical experiments for cooperative autonomous vehicles requires huge investments that can be prohibitive, creating a barrier for research and development in the field.
AI.method: Developed 1:10 scaled mini-cars equipped with Jetson Orin board running ROS2 for autonomous operations, Raspberry Pi with OScar (open source ETSI C-ITS compliant stack) for connectivity, enabling cooperative intelligent transport system testing.
AI.result: Successfully demonstrated feasibility through implementation and validation of Day-1 intersection collision warning (ICW) application using the scaled platform.
AI.conclusion: Scaled mini-cars with OScar provide a cost-effective intermediate testing platform for cooperative autonomous vehicle algorithms, bridging the gap between simulation and full-scale deployment while maintaining ETSI C-ITS compliance.

title: Safe Consensus of Cooperative Manipulation with Hierarchical Event-Triggered Control Barrier Functions
summary: Cooperative transport and manipulation of heavy or bulky payloads by multiple manipulators requires coordinated formation tracking, while simultaneously enforcing strict safety constraints in varying environments with limited communication and real-time computation budgets. This paper presents a distributed control framework that achieves consensus coordination with safety guarantees via hierarchical event-triggered control barrier functions (CBFs). We first develop a consensus-based protocol that relies solely on local neighbor information to enforce both translational and rotational consistency in task space. Building on this coordination layer, we propose a three-level hierarchical event-triggered safety architecture with CBFs, which is integrated with a risk-aware leader selection and smooth switching strategy to reduce online computation. The proposed approach is validated through real-world hardware experiments using two Franka manipulators operating with static obstacles, as well as comprehensive simulations demonstrating scalable multi-arm cooperation with dynamic obstacles. Results demonstrate higher precision cooperation under strict safety constraints, achieving substantially reduced computational cost and communication frequency compared to baseline methods.

AI.tldr: Distributed control framework for multi-manipulator cooperative transport with consensus coordination and hierarchical event-triggered safety guarantees using control barrier functions.
AI.motivation: Cooperative transport of heavy/bulky payloads requires coordinated formation tracking while enforcing strict safety constraints in varying environments with limited communication and real-time computation budgets.
AI.method: Three-level hierarchical event-triggered safety architecture with CBFs integrated with consensus-based coordination protocol using local neighbor information, plus risk-aware leader selection and smooth switching strategy.
AI.result: Higher precision cooperation under strict safety constraints with substantially reduced computational cost and communication frequency compared to baseline methods, validated through hardware experiments and simulations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed distributed control framework successfully enables safe, coordinated multi-manipulator cooperation with reduced computational and communication overhead through hierarchical event-triggered CBFs and consensus coordination.

title: Data Analogies Enable Efficient Cross-Embodiment Transfer
summary: Generalist robot policies are trained on demonstrations collected across a wide variety of robots, scenes, and viewpoints. Yet it remains unclear how to best organize and scale such heterogeneous data so that it genuinely improves performance in a given target setting. In this work, we ask: what form of demonstration data is most useful for enabling transfer across robot set-ups? We conduct controlled experiments that vary end-effector morphology, robot platform appearance, and camera perspective, and compare the effects of simply scaling the number of demonstrations against systematically broadening the diversity in different ways. Our simulated experiments show that while perceptual shifts such as viewpoint benefit most from broad diversity, morphology shifts benefit far less from unstructured diversity and instead see the largest gains from data analogies, i.e. paired demonstrations that align scenes, tasks, and/or trajectories across different embodiments. Informed by the simulation results, we improve real-world cross-embodiment transfer success by an average of $22.5\%$ over large-scale, unpaired datasets by changing only the composition of the data.

AI.tldr: Systematic investigation of demonstration data composition for cross-embodiment robot policy transfer, showing data analogies (paired demonstrations across embodiments) outperform unstructured diversity for morphology shifts.
AI.motivation: To determine the most effective form of demonstration data for enabling transfer across different robot set-ups (end-effector morphology, platform appearance, camera perspective) in generalist robot policies.
AI.method: Controlled experiments varying end-effector morphology, robot platform appearance, and camera perspective; comparing scaling demonstration quantity versus systematic diversity broadening; simulated experiments followed by real-world validation.
AI.result: Perceptual shifts (viewpoint) benefit most from broad diversity, while morphology shifts benefit far less from unstructured diversity and see largest gains from data analogies (paired demonstrations aligning scenes, tasks, trajectories across embodiments). Real-world cross-embodiment transfer improved by 22.5% over large-scale unpaired datasets by changing data composition.
AI.conclusion: Data composition matters more than simple scaling for cross-embodiment transfer; data analogies are particularly effective for morphology shifts, enabling significant real-world performance improvements through strategic data organization.

title: History-Conditioned Spatio-Temporal Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language Navigation
summary: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) enables robots to follow natural-language instructions in visually grounded environments, serving as a key capability for embodied robotic systems. Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong navigation performance, but their high computational cost introduces latency that limits real-time deployment. We propose a training-free spatio-temporal vision token pruning framework tailored to VLA-based VLN. We apply spatial token selection to the current view, alongside spatio-temporal compression for historical memories, enabling efficient long-horizon inference while reducing redundant computation. Leveraging attention-based token importance and query-guided spatio-temporal filtering, the proposed approach preserves navigation-relevant information without retraining or modifying pretrained models, allowing plug-and-play integration into existing VLA systems. Through experiments on standard VLN benchmarks, we confirm that our method significantly outperforms existing pruning strategies. It successfully preserves superior navigation accuracy under extreme pruning scenarios, all while maintaining the highly competitive inference efficiency. Real-world deployment on a Unitree Go2 quadruped robot further validates reliable and low-latency instruction-following navigation under practical robotic constraints. We hope this work helps bridge the gap between large-scale multimodal modeling and efficient, real-time embodied deployment in robotic navigation systems.

AI.tldr: Training-free spatio-temporal vision token pruning framework for Vision-Language-Action models that reduces computational latency while preserving navigation accuracy for real-time robotic deployment.
AI.motivation: Vision-Language-Action models have strong navigation performance but high computational cost limits real-time deployment. Need to bridge gap between large-scale multimodal modeling and efficient real-time embodied robotic systems.
AI.method: Training-free spatio-temporal vision token pruning framework with spatial token selection for current view and spatio-temporal compression for historical memories. Uses attention-based token importance and query-guided spatio-temporal filtering to preserve navigation-relevant information without retraining.
AI.result: Significantly outperforms existing pruning strategies on standard VLN benchmarks. Preserves superior navigation accuracy under extreme pruning scenarios while maintaining highly competitive inference efficiency. Validated on real-world Unitree Go2 quadruped robot with reliable low-latency navigation.
AI.conclusion: Proposed framework enables plug-and-play integration into existing VLA systems, bridging gap between large-scale multimodal modeling and efficient real-time embodied deployment in robotic navigation systems.

title: Control Barrier Corridors: From Safety Functions to Safe Sets
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, an extended preprint version of a conference paper
summary: Safe autonomy is a critical requirement and a key enabler for robots to operate safely in unstructured complex environments. Control barrier functions and safe motion corridors are two widely used but technically distinct safety methods, functional and geometric, respectively, for safe motion planning and control. Control barrier functions are applied to the safety filtering of control inputs to limit the decay rate of system safety, whereas safe motion corridors are geometrically constructed to define a local safe zone around the system state for use in motion optimization and reference-governor design. This paper introduces a new notion of control barrier corridors, which unifies these two approaches by converting control barrier functions into local safe goal regions for reference goal selection in feedback control systems. We show, with examples on fully actuated systems, kinematic unicycles, and linear output regulation systems, that individual state safety can be extended locally over control barrier corridors for convex barrier functions, provided the control convergence rate matches the barrier decay rate, highlighting a trade-off between safety and reactiveness. Such safe control barrier corridors enable safely reachable persistent goal selection over continuously changing barrier corridors during system motion, which we demonstrate for verifiably safe and persistent path following in autonomous exploration of unknown environments.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Control Barrier Corridors (CBCs) that unify control barrier functions (functional safety) and safe motion corridors (geometric safety) by converting barrier functions into local safe goal regions for reference-governor control.
AI.motivation: Safe autonomy requires robust safety methods for robots in unstructured environments. Existing approaches like control barrier functions (functional) and safe motion corridors (geometric) are technically distinct, creating a need for a unified framework that combines their strengths.
AI.method: Introduces Control Barrier Corridors (CBCs) that transform control barrier functions into local safe goal regions for reference goal selection in feedback control. The approach requires matching control convergence rate with barrier decay rate for convex barrier functions, enabling safe reachable persistent goal selection over continuously changing barrier corridors during motion.
AI.result: Demonstrates the approach on fully actuated systems, kinematic unicycles, and linear output regulation systems, showing that individual state safety can be extended locally over control barrier corridors. The method enables verifiably safe and persistent path following in autonomous exploration of unknown environments.
AI.conclusion: Control Barrier Corridors provide a unified framework that bridges functional and geometric safety approaches, enabling safe reachable persistent goal selection with a trade-off between safety and reactiveness. The method supports safe autonomous exploration in unknown environments through continuously adapting safe corridors.

title: A Unified Low-Dimensional Design Embedding for Joint Optimization of Shape, Material, and Actuation in Soft Robots
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: Soft robots achieve functionality through tight coupling among geometry, material composition, and actuation. As a result, effective design optimization requires these three aspects to be considered jointly rather than in isolation. This coupling is computationally challenging: nonlinear large-deformation mechanics increase simulation cost, while contact, collision handling, and non-smooth state transitions limit the applicability of standard gradient-based approaches. We introduce a smooth, low-dimensional design embedding for soft robots that unifies shape morphing, multi-material distribution, and actuation within a single structured parameter space. Shape variation is modeled through continuous deformation maps of a reference geometry, while material properties are encoded as spatial fields. Both are constructed from shared basis functions. This representation enables expressive co-design while drastically reducing the dimensionality of the search space. In our experiments, we show that design expressiveness increases with the number of basis functions, unlike comparable neural network encodings whose representational capacity does not scale predictably with parameter count. We further show that joint co-optimization of shape, material, and actuation using our unified embedding consistently outperforms sequential strategies. All experiments are performed independently of the underlying simulator, confirming compatibility with black-box simulation pipelines. Across multiple dynamic tasks, the proposed embedding surpasses neural network and voxel-based baseline parameterizations while using significantly fewer design parameters. Together, these findings demonstrate that structuring the design space itself enables efficient co-design of soft robots.

AI.tldr: A unified design embedding for soft robots that jointly optimizes shape, material distribution, and actuation using smooth, low-dimensional parameterization based on shared basis functions.
AI.motivation: Soft robot design requires joint consideration of geometry, material composition, and actuation due to tight coupling, but current approaches face computational challenges from nonlinear mechanics, contact handling, and non-smooth state transitions that limit gradient-based optimization.
AI.method: Introduces a smooth, low-dimensional design embedding using continuous deformation maps for shape variation and spatial fields for material properties, both constructed from shared basis functions. This unified representation enables joint co-design while reducing search space dimensionality.
AI.result: The proposed embedding shows increasing design expressiveness with more basis functions (unlike neural network encodings), consistently outperforms sequential optimization strategies, works with black-box simulators, and surpasses neural network and voxel-based baselines across dynamic tasks using fewer parameters.
AI.conclusion: Structuring the design space itself enables efficient co-design of soft robots by providing a unified, low-dimensional embedding that jointly optimizes shape, material, and actuation while maintaining compatibility with existing simulation pipelines.

title: CFEAR-Teach-and-Repeat: Fast and Accurate Radar-only Localization
comment: This paper has been accepted for publication in the IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), 2026
summary: Reliable localization in prior maps is essential for autonomous navigation, particularly under adverse weather, where optical sensors may fail. We present CFEAR-TR, a teach-and-repeat localization pipeline using a single spinning radar, which is designed for easily deployable, lightweight, and robust navigation in adverse conditions. Our method localizes by jointly aligning live scans to both stored scans from the teach mapping pass, and to a sliding window of recent live keyframes. This ensures accurate and robust pose estimation across different seasons and weather phenomena. Radar scans are represented using a sparse set of oriented surface points, computed from Doppler-compensated measurements. The map is stored in a pose graph that is traversed during localization. Experiments on the held-out test sequences from the Boreas dataset show that CFEAR-TR can localize with an accuracy as low as 0.117 m and 0.096°, corresponding to improvements of up to 63% over the previous state of the art, while running efficiently at 29 Hz. These results substantially narrow the gap to lidar-level localization, particularly in heading estimation. We make the C++ implementation of our work available to the community.

AI.tldr: CFEAR-TR is a teach-and-repeat localization pipeline using a single spinning radar that achieves lidar-level accuracy (0.117m, 0.096°) in adverse weather conditions, running at 29 Hz.
AI.motivation: Reliable localization in prior maps is essential for autonomous navigation under adverse weather conditions where optical sensors (like cameras) often fail. There's a need for robust, easily deployable navigation systems that can operate across different seasons and weather phenomena.
AI.method: A teach-and-repeat localization pipeline using a single spinning radar. The method localizes by jointly aligning live scans to both stored scans from the teach mapping pass and to a sliding window of recent live keyframes. Radar scans are represented using a sparse set of oriented surface points computed from Doppler-compensated measurements, and the map is stored in a pose graph that is traversed during localization.
AI.result: Experiments on the Boreas dataset show localization accuracy as low as 0.117 m and 0.096°, representing improvements of up to 63% over previous state-of-the-art methods. The system runs efficiently at 29 Hz and substantially narrows the gap to lidar-level localization, particularly in heading estimation.
AI.conclusion: CFEAR-TR provides a lightweight, robust, and easily deployable radar-based localization solution that achieves lidar-level accuracy in adverse weather conditions, making it suitable for autonomous navigation when optical sensors fail. The C++ implementation is made available to the community.

title: SG-DOR: Learning Scene Graphs with Direction-Conditioned Occlusion Reasoning for Pepper Plants
summary: Robotic harvesting in dense crop canopies requires effective interventions that depend not only on geometry, but also on explicit, direction-conditioned relations identifying which organs obstruct a target fruit. We present SG-DOR (Scene Graphs with Direction-Conditioned Occlusion Reasoning), a relational framework that, given instance-segmented organ point clouds, infers a scene graph encoding physical attachments and direction-conditioned occlusion. We introduce an occlusion ranking task for retrieving and ranking candidate leaves for a target fruit and approach direction, and propose a direction-aware graph neural architecture with per-fruit leaf-set attention and union-level aggregation. Experiments on a multi-plant synthetic pepper dataset show improved occlusion prediction (F1=0.73, NDCG@3=0.85) and attachment inference (edge F1=0.83) over strong ablations, yielding a structured relational signal for downstream intervention planning.

AI.tldr: SG-DOR is a relational framework using scene graphs with direction-conditioned occlusion reasoning for robotic harvesting in dense crop canopies, improving occlusion prediction and attachment inference.
AI.motivation: Robotic harvesting in dense crop canopies requires understanding not just geometry but also explicit, direction-conditioned relations to identify which organs obstruct target fruits during harvesting interventions.
AI.method: SG-DOR infers scene graphs from instance-segmented organ point clouds, encoding physical attachments and direction-conditioned occlusion. It introduces occlusion ranking for retrieving/ranking candidate leaves for target fruits and approach directions, using a direction-aware graph neural architecture with per-fruit leaf-set attention and union-level aggregation.
AI.result: Experiments on a multi-plant synthetic pepper dataset show improved occlusion prediction (F1=0.73, NDCG@3=0.85) and attachment inference (edge F1=0.83) over strong ablations, providing structured relational signals for downstream intervention planning.
AI.conclusion: SG-DOR effectively captures direction-conditioned occlusion relations and physical attachments in dense crop canopies, offering a structured relational framework to support robotic harvesting intervention planning.

title: Underactuated multimodal jumping robot for extraterrestrial exploration
summary: We present a rolling and jumping underactuated monopedal robot designed to explore multimodal locomotion on low-gravity bodies. It uses only two reaction wheels to control its spatial orientation with two controllers: a balancing controller which can aim the robot's jump direction on the ground, and an aerial reorientation controller which can aim the robot's leg for landing after flight. We demonstrate rolling, targeted jumping and landing, and self-righting using only three actuators total, keeping system size to 0.33m and 1.25kg. Simple switching between locomotion modes enables the system to deal with differing landscapes and environmental conditions.

AI.tldr: A two-wheel underactuated monopedal robot achieves multimodal locomotion (rolling, targeted jumping/landing, self-righting) on low-gravity bodies using only three actuators.
AI.motivation: To explore multimodal locomotion capabilities for robotic exploration of low-gravity planetary bodies (asteroids, small moons) with minimal actuation and system complexity.
AI.method: Uses two reaction wheels for spatial orientation control with two controllers: ground balancing controller for jump direction targeting, and aerial reorientation controller for leg landing alignment. Simple switching between locomotion modes enables adaptation to different terrains.
AI.result: Demonstrated rolling, targeted jumping and landing, and self-righting capabilities with only three actuators total, achieving compact system size (0.33m, 1.25kg).
AI.conclusion: The underactuated design with minimal actuators enables effective multimodal locomotion for low-gravity exploration, demonstrating that simple mode switching can handle diverse terrain conditions.

title: Unified Learning of Temporal Task Structure and Action Timing for Bimanual Robot Manipulation
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: Temporal task structure is fundamental for bimanual manipulation: a robot must not only know that one action precedes or overlaps another, but also when each action should occur and how long it should take. While symbolic temporal relations enable high-level reasoning about task structure and alternative execution sequences, concrete timing parameters are equally essential for coordinating two hands at the execution level. Existing approaches address these two levels in isolation, leaving a gap between high-level task planning and low-level movement synchronization. This work presents an approach for learning both symbolic and subsymbolic temporal task constraints from human demonstrations and deriving executable, temporally parametrized plans for bimanual manipulation. Our contributions are (i) a 3-dimensional representation of timings between two actions with methods based on multivariate Gaussian Mixture Models to represent temporal relationships between actions on a subsymbolic level, (ii) a method based on the Davis-Putnam-Logemann-Loveland (DPLL) algorithm that finds and ranks all contradiction-free assignments of Allen relations to action pairs, representing different modes of a task, and (iii) an optimization-based planning system that combines the identified symbolic and subsymbolic temporal task constraints to derive temporally parametrized plans for robot execution. We evaluate our approach on several datasets, demonstrating that our method generates temporally parametrized plans closer to human demonstrations than the most characteristic demonstration baseline.

AI.tldr: A method for learning both symbolic (Allen relations) and subsymbolic (timing parameters) temporal constraints from human demonstrations to generate executable, temporally parametrized plans for bimanual manipulation.
AI.motivation: Temporal structure is crucial for bimanual manipulation, requiring both high-level symbolic reasoning about action sequences and low-level timing parameters for coordination. Existing approaches address these levels in isolation, creating a gap between task planning and movement synchronization.
AI.method: Three-part approach: (1) 3D timing representation using multivariate Gaussian Mixture Models for subsymbolic temporal relationships; (2) DPLL-based method to find and rank contradiction-free Allen relation assignments representing task modes; (3) optimization-based planning combining symbolic and subsymbolic constraints to derive temporally parametrized plans.
AI.result: Evaluation on several datasets shows the method generates temporally parametrized plans closer to human demonstrations than the most characteristic demonstration baseline.
AI.conclusion: The approach successfully bridges the gap between high-level symbolic task planning and low-level movement synchronization by learning both symbolic and subsymbolic temporal constraints from demonstrations, enabling executable bimanual manipulation plans.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Dynamics For Underwater Vehicle-Manipulator Robots
summary: Accurate and adaptive dynamic models are critical for underwater vehicle-manipulator systems where hydrodynamic effects induce time-varying parameters. This paper introduces a novel uncertainty-aware adaptive dynamics model framework that remains linear in lumped vehicle and manipulator parameters, and embeds convex physical consistency constraints during online estimation. Moving horizon estimation is used to stack horizon regressors, enforce realizable inertia, damping, friction, and hydrostatics, and quantify uncertainty from parameter evolution. Experiments on a BlueROV2 Heavy with a 4-DOF manipulator demonstrate rapid convergence and calibrated predictions. Manipulator fits achieve R2 = 0.88 to 0.98 with slopes near unity, while vehicle surge, heave, and roll are reproduced with good fidelity under stronger coupling and noise. Median solver time is approximately 0.023 s per update, confirming online feasibility. A comparison against a fixed parameter model shows consistent reductions in MAE and RMSE across degrees of freedom. Results indicate physically plausible parameters and confidence intervals with near 100% coverage, enabling reliable feedforward control and simulation in underwater environments.

AI.tldr: Novel uncertainty-aware adaptive dynamics model for underwater vehicle-manipulator systems using moving horizon estimation with physical consistency constraints, enabling online parameter estimation with quantified uncertainty.
AI.motivation: Underwater vehicle-manipulator systems require accurate dynamic models, but hydrodynamic effects cause time-varying parameters. Existing approaches lack uncertainty quantification and physical consistency guarantees during online adaptation.
AI.method: Uncertainty-aware adaptive dynamics framework that remains linear in lumped parameters, embeds convex physical consistency constraints (inertia, damping, friction, hydrostatics), and uses moving horizon estimation to stack horizon regressors and quantify parameter evolution uncertainty.
AI.result: Experimental validation on BlueROV2 Heavy with 4-DOF manipulator: R² = 0.88-0.98 for manipulator fits, good fidelity for vehicle surge/heave/roll under coupling/noise, median solver time ~0.023s per update, consistent MAE/RMSE reductions vs fixed parameter model, physically plausible parameters with near 100% confidence interval coverage.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables reliable feedforward control and simulation in underwater environments through physically consistent online parameter adaptation with quantified uncertainty, demonstrating practical feasibility for real-time applications.
